title: Bài sưu tầm 127 - Passage 1: The Monarch Butterfly: An Epic Across Generations
passageHtml:
READING PASSAGE 1 — TEST 127

The Monarch Butterfly: An Epic Across Generations

Paragraph 1. Each autumn, millions of monarch butterflies embark on one of the most extraordinary long-distance migrations in the insect world. Weighing less than half a gram, these orange-and-black insects travel up to 4,000 kilometres from southern Canada and the northern United States to a handful of mountain forests in central Mexico. Their survival during this hazardous journey owes much to what they eat early in life. Female monarchs lay eggs exclusively on milkweed plants, and hatching caterpillars feed solely on milkweed leaves, absorbing bitter chemical compounds known as cardenolides. These stored toxins remain inside the adult butterfly's tissues, making it deeply unpleasant and potentially sickening for birds to eat.

Paragraph 2. Most summer-born monarchs live for barely five weeks, breeding quickly and dying near their birthplace. However, triggered by cooling northern winds and diminishing daylight, the final autumn generation emerges in a radically different biological state. Its reproductive organs remain temporarily inactive, allowing energy to be diverted into fat reserves for flight. Instead of surviving for weeks, this migratory generation lives up to eight months. Scientists have discovered that monarchs orient southward using a sun compass tuned by circadian clocks in their antennae, while relying on an internal sensor sensitive to Earth's magnetism whenever overcast skies hide the sun.

Paragraph 3. Although millions of butterflies vanished northward and southward every year, their exact winter refuge remained a mystery to researchers until 1975, when Canadian zoologist Fred Urquhart and a network of volunteer taggers traced labelled insects to the high volcanic ridges of Michoacán in Mexico. At elevations above 3,000 metres, tens of millions of monarchs drape themselves over oyamel fir trees in dense clusters that shield the insects against freezing night air.

Paragraph 4. Even inside this high-altitude shelter, winter weather can prove fatal. A dry frost rarely kills resting butterflies, yet soaking winter rain followed by a sudden drop in temperature can wipe out millions of dormant insects overnight. Meanwhile, illegal logging along the edges of the protected reserve thins the dense evergreen canopy that normally acts as a blanket over the colonies.

Paragraph 5. Unlike migratory birds, no individual monarch completes the full round trip. As spring warmth arrives in March, survivors mate and fly north into Texas and neighbouring states, where females lay eggs on emerging milkweed before dying. Three or four consecutive generations must hatch, mature, and push farther north before the summer descendants finally reach the northern United States and Canada. How the distant descendants of autumn migrants locate the exact Mexican hillsides visited by their great-great-grandparents remains an enduring puzzle.

Paragraph 6. Over the past two decades, eastern monarch numbers have fallen sharply. Across North America's agricultural belt, the widespread spraying of herbicides on modern farm fields has eradicated vast stretches of wild milkweed where females once laid eggs. Conservationists now urge homeowners, schools, and highway agencies to plant native milkweed corridors to keep this multi-generational journey alive.

groups.title: Questions 8–13
groups.instructions:
Do the following statements agree with the information given in Reading Passage 1?
In boxes 8–13 on your answer sheet, write TRUE, FALSE or NOT GIVEN.

steps: Đoạn 1: "These stored toxins remain inside the adult butterfly's tissues, making it deeply unpleasant... for birds to eat."
Từ cần điền: toxins.
Đoạn 2: "...triggered by cooling northern winds and diminishing daylight..."
Từ cần điền: daylight.
Đoạn 2: "...relying on an internal sensor sensitive to Earth's magnetism whenever overcast skies hide the sun."
Từ cần điền: magnetism.
Đoạn 3: "...drape themselves over oyamel fir trees in dense clusters that shield the insects against freezing night air."
Từ cần điền: clusters.
Đoạn 4: "...soaking winter rain followed by a sudden drop in temperature can wipe out millions..."
Từ cần điền: rain.
Đoạn 5: "Three or four consecutive generations must hatch, mature, and push farther north..."
Từ cần điền: generations.
Đoạn 6: "...the widespread spraying of herbicides on modern farm fields has eradicated vast stretches of wild milkweed..."
Từ cần điền: herbicides.

q8.text: Birds avoid eating adult monarch butterflies because of substances the insects obtained before reaching adulthood.

steps: Đoạn 1: Sâu bướm hấp thụ hợp chất từ cây bông tai (milkweed) và chất độc đó lưu lại trong mô bướm trưởng thành khiến chim không dám ăn.
Kết luận: Chọn TRUE.

q9.text: Local communities in Michoacán receive government payments to protect oyamel fir trees from illegal logging.

steps: Đoạn 4: Có nhắc đến vùng bảo tồn và nạn chặt phá rừng trái phép (illegal logging), nhưng không hề đề cập việc cộng đồng địa phương nhận tiền trợ cấp chính phủ.
Kết luận: Chọn NOT GIVEN.

q10.text: Monarch butterflies rely exclusively on the position of the sun to maintain their southward direction.

steps: Đoạn 2: Ngoài la bàn mặt trời, khi trời u ám bướm còn dùng cảm biến từ trường Trái Đất (Earth's magnetism), không phải chỉ dựa hoàn toàn (exclusively) vào mặt trời.
Kết luận: Chọn FALSE.

q11.text: Extreme cold alone is less dangerous to resting monarchs than cold combined with moisture.

steps: Đoạn 4: Băng giá khô hiếm khi gây chết (dry frost rarely kills), nhưng mưa ẩm kèm rét đậm có thể xóa sổ hàng triệu con.
Kết luận: Chọn TRUE.

q12.text: Citizen volunteers tagged more than one million butterflies during Fred Urquhart's research project.

steps: Đoạn 3: Có nhắc Fred Urquhart và mạng lưới tình nguyện viên gắn thẻ bướm, nhưng không có số liệu cụ thể về số lượng bướm đã gắn thẻ.
Kết luận: Chọn NOT GIVEN.

q13.text: Individual butterflies that survive winter in Mexico fly all the way back to Canada the following summer.

steps: Đoạn 5: Không cá thể nào hoàn thành cả vòng khứ hồi; bướm sống sót đẻ trứng ở miền nam Mỹ rồi chết, cần 3–4 thế hệ nối tiếp mới về tới Canada.
Kết luận: Chọn FALSE.
